answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost.
